Here, perfect straight lines were obtained, if the In(OD 600) values were plotted against the squared times (Fig. 3A, inset). As outlined in in the supplemental material, this implies that the specific growth during the lag phase increases linearly in time (Fig. 1B and 2B). Also, the specific methane-forming activity increased linearly in time during this period (Fig. 1B and 2B). The specific growth rates became maximal at the entry of the exponential stage and remained constant throughout the particular stage (Fig. 1B, 2B, and 3A). The values did not significantly differ among the various gassing regimens (0.22 to 0.25 h; doubling times of 2.8 to 3.1 h) (Table 3). However, the 9cH, was not constant. The decline occurred concomitant with the deerease in the dissolved hydrogen partial pressures, resulting from the increasing hydrogen uptake rates by the growing biomass (Fig. 1 and 2 and Table 3). Apparently, the physiology of the cells continnously changed, even at a constant growth rate. After exponential growth, the cells entered the linear phase.
